PEOPLE-POWERED TOURISM HOST MODEL
How People Participate in Tourism
Purpose

The People-Powered Tourism Host Model establishes a people-centred approach to tourism participation, recognising the Host as an important connection between visitors, people, places and tourism experiences.

It provides a flexible model through which individuals, families, communities, enterprises and Host Teams can participate in tourism by welcoming visitors, providing care, sharing knowledge, facilitating experiences and contributing to meaningful visitor connections.
People-Powered Hosting
Tourism is ultimately experienced through people.
A place may provide the setting, but it is often the people visitors meet, the stories they hear, the care they receive and the connections they make that shape the experience.
The People-Powered Tourism Host Model therefore places people at the heart of tourism participation.
A Host is a person who welcomes, connects with, cares for, guides, engages with or facilitates visitors during a stay, experience, journey or other tourism activity.
Hosting may be undertaken by an individual or by a Host Team, where two or more people work together to deliver the human and practical aspects of a tourism offering.

The Host Model creates opportunities for more people to participate directly in tourism and for their knowledge, skills, culture, hospitality and local connections to become part of the visitor experience.
Why the Host Model Matters
Tourism creates value not only through products and places, but through human connection.
The Host Model helps transform local participation into meaningful tourism value by creating opportunities for people to contribute according to their capabilities, interests and circumstances.
It can enable:
individuals to participate in tourism through their skills, knowledge and hospitality;
families and communities to participate collectively;
tourism enterprises to create stronger and more personal visitor connections;
local knowledge and culture to become part of authentic visitor experiences;
Stay Developers to strengthen the human dimension of stays;
Experience Creators to work with people who can bring experiences to life; and
different participants to collaborate through Host Teams.
In this way, hosting becomes more than a service function. It becomes a pathway for participation, enterprise development, shared value and shared prosperity.
The People-Powered Tourism Host Model
The Host Model can be applied across different forms of tourism participation.

Within Stays, a Stay Host or Host Team may welcome guests, communicate with visitors, provide guest care, undertake housekeeping, prepare or serve meals where provided, care for the property and help guests connect with the surrounding people and place.

Within Experiences, an Experience Host may welcome and facilitate visitors, share knowledge and stories, guide activities, demonstrate skills, or help create meaningful connections with people and place.

Within Journeys, destinations and other tourism activities, Hosts may contribute through guiding, interpretation, culinary knowledge, cultural knowledge, wellness, nature, agriculture, crafts, education, community engagement or other forms of expertise and participation.
The model is intentionally flexible. The nature of hosting may differ according to the tourism offering, the people involved and the responsibilities they undertake.
Hosts and Host Teams
A Host may participate independently, as part of a tourism enterprise, family, community or other organisation.
A tourism offering may also be delivered by a Host Team, bringing together people with complementary responsibilities, knowledge and skills.
For example:
Stay Developer → Stay Host / Host Team → Visitor
Experience Creator → Experience Host / Host Team → Visitor
The Creator and Host may be the same person, or they may be different people.
This flexibility allows tourism enterprises and local communities to organise participation according to their own capabilities, resources and circumstances.

The Host is therefore recognised as a distinct tourism participation role rather than being defined solely by an employment relationship. The specific nature of participation, compensation and responsibilities may be established through appropriate agreements and applicable legal requirements.
Hosting Across the Tourism Ecosystem
The Host Model is not limited to accommodation.
It can support participation across the wider tourism ecosystem, including:

Stays
Welcoming and caring for visitors within distinctive accommodation.

Experiences
Facilitating meaningful activities, stories, knowledge and connections.

Journeys
Supporting visitors through guiding, interpretation, local knowledge and personal connection.

Culture & Heritage
Sharing traditions, stories, skills, practices and living heritage.

Nature & Adventure
Connecting visitors with landscapes, environments, activities and local knowledge.

Food & Wellness
Sharing culinary traditions, local produce, wellness practices and knowledge.

Community & Learning
Creating opportunities for visitors to learn from and connect with local people and communities.
Through these different forms of participation, the Host Model helps connect tourism demand with people who can create meaningful value.
From Hosting to Shared Value
When people participate in tourism, they contribute knowledge, skills, time, care, relationships, resources and local connections.
The Host Model recognises these contributions as part of the value created through tourism.

This connects naturally with the People-Powered Tourism Revenue Sharing Model, through which tourism revenue can be shared among participating parties according to their roles, responsibilities, contributions and agreed value creation.
The underlying pathway is:
Participation → Contribution → Tourism Value → Shared Revenue → Shared Prosperity
This creates a stronger connection between participation and economic opportunity, helping ensure that tourism value can flow to the people who contribute to creating it.
Embedding the Host Model in the Framework
The People-Powered Tourism Host Model is one of the three main model categories within the People-Powered Tourism Framework.
It can be applied across the Framework's Strategic Pillars, Development Models and Operational Platforms, adapting to the nature of each tourism activity.

Through the model, Traveleye Alliance can help create pathways for people to participate in tourism, develop their capabilities, contribute to tourism enterprises and experiences, and share in the value created through tourism.
The Host Model therefore strengthens the Framework's central commitment to building tourism through People, Place, Partnerships and Purpose.
From Model to Practice
The Host Model provides a common foundation while allowing each tourism enterprise, community, stay, experience or destination to develop its own appropriate hosting approach.
Implementation can progressively develop through:

Identify
People with the interest, knowledge, skills or capacity to participate as Hosts.

Enable
Provide appropriate knowledge, skills, support and opportunities for participation.

Develop
Strengthen Hosts, Host Teams, tourism enterprises and tourism offerings.

Connect
Connect Hosts with visitors, tourism enterprises, destinations and wider ecosystem partners.

Share
Recognise contributions and enable appropriate revenue sharing and shared value creation.
Through this process, hosting can become a practical pathway for people to enter, participate in and grow within Sri Lanka's tourism ecosystem.
Looking Ahead

The People-Powered Tourism Host Model creates a foundation for a more participatory tourism ecosystem—one where visitors are welcomed not only by businesses, but by people with stories, knowledge, skills, culture and connections to share.

By enabling individuals, families, communities, tourism entrepreneurs and Host Teams to participate meaningfully, the model helps transform tourism from something delivered to people and places into something created with them.
The opportunity is to build a tourism ecosystem where more people can participate, more local value can be created, and more tourism prosperity can be shared.
